channel.title: The Year — The Earthly Book of Hours
channel.description: The year a day at a time, as kept in the Boston Basin: a subject of the season each day, with an image and a reading, and each week its Lectio Terra essay. It comes round again every year.

item.title: Lectio Terra: Fen and Wetland
item.description:
Charles Kinglsey, Amy Lowell, Arielle Kaplan, John Clare

While fall may be the season of the woodlands, the transition into winter can shift plant and animal activity toward the lower, tighter structure of all those water-adjacent landforms: fens, marshlands, bogs, mires and quagmires, swamps, sloughs, and swales—not to mention bayous, pocosins, and the many other regional variations of wetlands. If you’ve never stopped to wonder how these terms relate…

item.title: Lectio Terra: Eastern Grey Squirrel
item.description:
Meriwether Lewis, John Burroughs, Ralph Waldo Emerson

My brother called them “joeys” and “jojos” as a child, for reasons that escape me. Maybe he was thinking of young marsupials or mispronouncing the word “chipmunk.” At any rate, squirrels were one of the first forms of wildlife detectable through our family’s windows, in our backyard, or at the playgrounds we frequented. Like many suburban households, our closest neighbors were likely not people…
